subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <s.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Sarah — really useful conversation. Recapping the key points and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan.

High-level pain & goals
- Pain: inconsistent inference latency during peak batch scoring (esp. >1k concurrent requests), and high unit cost on the current vendor.
- Goal: reduce 95th_pct latency to <300ms for inference flows with streaming enabled, and lower per-embedding cost by ~30% through batching and quantization.
- Security: SOC 2 + VPC/private deployment required for PII-sensitive workflows.

Integration & product fit notes
- Primary integration: server-side Node/TypeScript SDK to drive both streaming responses (user-facing chat) and function/tool-calling for structured fulfillment.
- Function calling: we discussed using Redwood's function-calling shim to emit normalized JSON payloads (order:create, invoice:match).
- Streaming: Redwood supports chunked streaming and token-level progress for UI; this will allow your UX to show partial answers and reduce perceived latency.
- Structured outputs & reranking: plan to use structured outputs for downstream parsers and embeddings + reranker for candidate ordering in search. We'll recommend embedding model + a lightweight reranker for 1–5 candidate rescoring.
- SDK changes: small server-side wrapper for your existing scoring pipeline; we can ship an example with function-calling types and streaming handlers.

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA)
1) Marissa: share SDK integration guide + sample Node app (attached) — by EOD Mon 2027-04-12.
2) Acme (Sarah/Miguel): share sample dataset and expected QPS patterns, including current latency p95 baseline — by Wed 2027-04-14.
3) Rishi: scope a short POC (2-week) with a reserved test pool and demo tokens for eval — draft proposal by Thu 2027-04-15.
4) Stephanie: prepare a security checklist and SOC2 onboarding notes for your infra team.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf (integration examples), acme-mop-proposal.xlsx (MOP/initial sizing).

If that captures everything, we can lock in a technical kickoff next Tue (2027-04-13) to walk engineers through the SDK and function-calling examples.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Sarah Johnson <s.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 16:12:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and matches our notes. A couple quick follow-ups from our side:

- Embedding latency: for similarity search we need 95th_pct embed latency <200ms for single-item embedding requests. Can we confirm which models / quantization profiles meet that in your hosted offering or Dedicated pool?
- Security: SOC2 is a hard requirement; can Stephanie share the onboarding checklist and any timelines for Private deployment? We may need a VPC-backed option.
- Function calling: curious about validation/typing — do you provide TypeScript types or schema enforcement for function call outputs? That would reduce parsing errors on our side.

Also adding Miguel (platform) to loop on QPS numbers — he can attach the traffic spreadsheet.

Happy to do the technical kickoff on Tue — Miguel prefers a 10am PT slot.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Search & AI
Acme Corp

Thanks — noted on the questions. Quick answers and what I'm attaching:

- Embedding latency: our recommended embedding models for low-latency single-item calls are the r-infer-embed-medium and r-infer-embed-fast (quantized profiles available). In our Dedicated pools we can guarantee lower variance; I'll ask Rishi to include the perf matrix in the POC doc.
- Security & Private deployment: Stephanie is copying a SOC2 onboarding checklist. For VPC/on-prem we have a standard timeline (2–6 weeks depending on network approvals); we'll surface exact gating items in the checklist.
- Function calling & types: we provide TypeScript types for function schemas in the SDK and runtime validation hooks. The sample Node repo includes a function-calling example with TypeScript interfaces.

Attachments included: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf (sample Node app, streaming handler, function schema examples), acme-mop-proposal.xlsx (initial sizing + estimated reserved capacity).

Proposed next meeting: Tue 2027-04-13 10:00 AM PT — technical kickoff (30–45m). If that works I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda (SDK walkthrough, POC scope, security kickoff).

Thanks again — we look forward to the POC.

Marissa
